name: slack
description: Golden support-question cases derived from the authly codebase, exercised through the Slack event source. Tests error diagnosis, API usage, and version-specific limitations across different documentation sources.

cases.name: permission-denied-authorization-error
cases.input: I'm calling permissions.check() and getting AuthorizationError: user 'usr_123' lacks permission 'documents:write'. The user exists and has roles assigned. What's wrong?
cases.expected_output: The error means none of the roles assigned to the user contain the exact permission string 'documents:write'. Permission names are case-sensitive ('documents:write' ≠ 'documents:Write'). To diagnose: 1) Inspect held permissions via authly.permissions.list_for_user(user_id=user.id), 2) Compare the actual permission strings against 'documents:write', 3) Assign a missing role or extend an existing one with the correct permission. Note: this error also appears for unknown user IDs because they have no assigned roles.

evidence.excerpt: Cause: none of the roles assigned to the user contains the requested permission string. Permission names must match exactly (documents:write ≠ documents:Write). Fix: inspect what the user actually holds via authly.permissions.list_for_user(user_id=user.id). Note: this error also appears for unknown user IDs because an unknown user has no assigned roles.
authly.permissions.check(user_id=user.id, permission='documents:write') raises AuthorizationError if not allowed.
AuthorizationError raised by permissions.check() when no assigned role contains the requested permission. Error format: user 'usr_...' lacks permission 'documents:write'.
